meta.title: Multi-tenant SaaS
meta.summary: One product serving thousands of customer organizations: shared pool for most tenants, dedicated silo for enterprise, strict isolation for all.

functional: Many customer organizations (tenants) use the same product
Each tenant only ever sees its own data
Enterprise tenants can get dedicated infrastructure
nonFunctional: No cross-tenant data leaks, even with an application bug
One noisy tenant cannot slow down others
Onboard a new tenant in minutes

nodes.label: API Gateway
nodes.description: Verifies tokens, resolves the tenant, applies per-tenant limits

nodes.label: Identity Provider
nodes.description: OIDC; tokens carry a tenant_id claim

nodes.label: App Service
nodes.description: Shared, stateless; never trusts a tenant id from the client

nodes.label: Tenant Catalog
nodes.description: tenant → plan, tier (pool / silo), database, limits

nodes.label: Pooled DB
nodes.description: All small tenants; every table has tenant_id with row-level security

nodes.label: Acme Dedicated DB
nodes.description: One enterprise tenant; own encryption key

flows.title: Request from a pooled tenant
flows.summary: Tenant comes from the verified token, limits come from the catalog, and the database itself enforces isolation.

steps.label: resolve globex.app.com
steps.detail: A wildcard record sends every tenant subdomain to the same entry point.

steps.label: GET /api/projects
steps.payload:
GET /api/projects HTTP/2
Host: globex.app.com
Authorization: Bearer eyJ…  (claims: sub=u_17, tenant_id=globex)

steps.label: verify JWT
steps.detail: Usually a local signature check with cached public keys. The tenant comes from the signed token, never from a header or body field the client controls.

steps.label: valid, tenant=globex
steps.detail: The gateway also checks the token's tenant matches the subdomain.

steps.label: GET tenant globex
steps.detail: Cached at the gateway for a minute.

steps.label: per-tenant rate limit
steps.detail: Noisy-neighbor protection: a tenant over its limit gets 429s; everyone else is unaffected.

steps.label: + tenant context
steps.detail: Forwarded as a signed internal header so services cannot be tricked by a client-supplied value.

steps.label: GET globex:projects
steps.detail: Every cache key is prefixed with the tenant id.

steps.label: SELECT with RLS
steps.detail: Row-level security: even if a query forgets WHERE tenant_id = …, the database only returns this tenant's rows.
steps.payload:
SET app.tenant_id = 'globex';
SELECT id, name FROM projects;   -- policy: tenant_id = current_setting('app.tenant_id')

flows.title: Request from an enterprise tenant
flows.summary: Same code path; the catalog routes Acme to its dedicated database and workers.

steps.label: POST /api/exports
steps.payload:
POST /api/exports HTTP/2
Host: acme.app.com
Authorization: Bearer eyJ…  (claims: tenant_id=acme)

steps.label: INSERT export job
steps.detail: Connection chosen from the catalog entry. The app code is identical for pooled and siloed tenants.

steps.label: job_9
steps.detail: Acme's heavy exports run on Acme's own workers, so they never compete with pooled tenants.

notes.text: Pool (shared everything) is cheapest and easiest to operate. Silo (dedicated per tenant) gives the strongest isolation and per-tenant tuning at higher cost. Most products pool by default and silo enterprise customers.
Defense in depth: tenant from the signed token, tenant-scoped connections, and row-level security in the database, so one forgotten WHERE clause cannot leak data.
Because routing comes from the catalog, a tenant that outgrows the pool can be migrated to its own database by copying data and flipping its catalog entry.
Per-tenant limits and per-tenant queues contain incidents: one tenant's runaway script cannot exhaust shared capacity.
Enterprise silos often get customer-managed encryption keys and a dedicated network for compliance.
